title: Optimize Console: cache orchestration & batching econ demo - Helio Systems
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran an Optimize console walkthrough focused on cache orchestration, batching tradeoffs, and a simple cost model for Helio's conversational product. Key themes: session vs prefix caching, expected hit rates, concurrency impact on batching, and dedicated vs hosted deployment considerations for latency and P95 SLOs.
next_steps: Alex to send tailored cost model spreadsheet and console access (due 2027-05-21)
Maya to share 1-week traffic heatmap and sample prompts (due 2027-05-20)
Schedule follow-up POC scoping call to run a 48-hour savings sandbox (tentative 2027-05-26)
Priya to propose KV caching TTL recommendations in Confluence doc
action_items: Alex - email cost model + sample RBAC doc by 2027-05-21
Maya - upload traffic heatmap and sample prompt set by 2027-05-20
Dan - check network egress constraints for private deployment and report back by 2027-05-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez, Priya Kapoor, Samir Lee (Redwood); Jordan Price, Maya Chen, Dan Flores, Talia Gomez (Helio)

[00:00] Alex: okay great, thanks everyone for joining. i'm alex from redwood inference, i'll run the deck briefly and priya will jump into the optimize console demo.
[00:14] Jordan: thanks, yeah we've been excited to see the cost savings you mentioned in the intro.
[00:18] Priya: awesome. quick agenda real quick — 1) traffic profile review, 2) batching + cache playbook overview, 3) run a few console sims with your numbers, 4) Q&A and next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Maya: yep that's perfect, we'll keep interruptions to questions.
[00:34] Priya: cool. jordan — could you give a 60-second on your product shape and constraints?
[00:39] Jordan: sure. Helio is customer support conversational AI, multi-tenant. peak qps 350 across regions, average prompt length about 420 tokens, median response 180 tokens. sessions are user-id tied, we do short-term context + long-term user profile. latency target p95 < 450ms for production.
[01:05] Priya: perfect, that helps. two immediate levers we usually look at: batching/concurrency configuration, and KV cache strategy (we'll call it prefix cache here). for your workload, the big knobs are: batch size distribution, per-session affinity, and the prefix length you can reliably cache.
[01:32] Samir: i'll add, in Optimize we attempt to auto-suggest a config but it's guided — you can run sims with your traffic and see cost delta.
[01:40] Maya: great, how do you model the cache hit rate? that's been fuzzy in other vendors.
[01:45] Priya: good question. we estimate hit rate based on repeated prefix occurrences in your sample prompt set, but also support user-defined heuristics. e.g., if you cache first 64 tokens of an instruction and your prompt set repeats the instruction 55% of the time, initial hit rate ~55%. we also simulate decay — TTL and eviction — to show long-term effects.
[02:10] Dan: when you say prefix cache do you mean the first tokens of the input, or also kv for session continuations?
[02:15] Priya: both patterns exist. prefix cache = common instruction + system prompt fragments; session KV = per-user cached kv of previous tokens for long conversational history. the platform handles both, but economics differ: session KV can give high hit rates but requires sticky session affinity and memory.
[02:36] Alex: let's fire up the console. i'm sharing my screen — Optimize > Simulations > New Sandbox. i'll load Helio's sample profile we preloaded.
[02:48] [screen share noise]
[03:00] Priya: okay i have your baseline: no cache, conservative batching (max batch 4, avg batch 2.1), hosted mode cost estimate $0.097 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.012 per 1k generated tokens — that's normalized from the model profile. baseline monthly burn estimate $42k for the sample traffic.
[03:25] Jordan: okay, that's inline with our internal calc. what's next?
[03:28] Priya: first sim: small prefix cache — cache first 64 tokens of system+instruction across tenants. we assume 48% hit rate on inference calls and TTL 10 minutes. simulate with same batching config. result: token cost down 12% and effective throughput improved, p95 drops ~40ms on average because the backend spends less decoding.
[03:56] Maya: 12% is interesting. how sensitive is that to hit rate?
[04:00] Priya: very — i'll toggle hit rate slider. if hit rate drops to 30%, cost savings shrink to 7%; at 70% hit rate, savings go to 18% and you can push batch max to 6 to get even better GPU efficiency.
[04:22] Dan: pushing batch max — won't that harm p95? we need to keep that 450ms cap.
[04:27] Priya: correct, so Optimize sim also shows latency CDFs. with larger batches you'll see slightly higher median but often similar p95 if you tune batching window; continuous batching helps reduce queuing. in the sim for your traffic, moving to max batch 6 with an adaptive micro-window kept p95 within 25ms of baseline because we had prefix hits removing tokens to generate.
[04:49] Alex: note — sample sizes matter. your workload has high peak short-term bursts. we recommend session-affinity for KV cache to avoid cross-shard misses when you need session history. that's easiest on Dedicated or Private.
[05:05] Jordan: good point. we're leaning hosted for first 3 months, then dedicated if numbers make sense. any guardrails?
[05:12] Samir: yes — in hosted mode we provide a fallback routing policy so that if dedicated capacity isn't available or cache miss spike occurs, you still route to compatible model variant. also we surface cost spikes on the console.
[05:23] Maya: can you show an example where we use both session KV and prefix? like hybrid?
[05:29] Priya: sure, let's run hybrid sim — prefix first 64 tokens + session KV for last 512 tokens when session affinity is enabled. assuming session sticky at 80% of requests after initial handshake. running...
[05:45] [simulation running noise]
[06:02] Priya: results: combined approach yields 28% cost reduction vs baseline, p95 down ~60ms, and GPU utilization improved ~1.9x which matters for reserved capacity. but memory footprint increases on the serving nodes because you're storing per-session kv.
[06:22] Dan: what's the memory per session estimate? we need to cap memory otherwise we'll OOM at scale.
[06:27] Priya: good call — Optimize reports estimated KV memory ~1.2KB per active session for your average history length; multiply by active sessions. with 30k active sessions that's ~36MB, which is fine per GPU node; but if you increase history to 4k tokens that estimate jumps.
[06:47] Jordan: how accurate are these memory estimates? we had a vendor underestimate before.
[06:51] Priya: they are conservative; they're generated from model kv size heuristics and monitored telemetry across runs. we recommend running a 48-hour sandbox to validate — that's why we propose the POC.
[07:05] Talia: security question — if we cache user profiles, what's the encryption-at-rest and keys model?
[07:11] Alex: for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we offer per-tenant envelope encryption. hosted mode uses Redwood-managed KMS but we can establish key-wrapping contracts for enterprise. we also emit audit logs for KV read/write.
[07:28] Maya: do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation?
[07:31] Samir: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we'll share the security pack after the call.
[07:38] Dan: if we went dedicated, could we pin model variants with quantized runtimes? we want lower cost but preserve quality.
[07:45] Priya: absolutely. Optimize will recommend quantization profiles where quality delta is small for your evaluation prompts. we also do A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to full-precision model if quality regressions are detected.
[07:58] Jordan: can you run a what-if where we add a conservative prefetch layer — precompute likely completions for top-5 intents?
[08:06] Priya: yes — that's lookahead prefetch (we sometimes call it precompute). sim: precomputation increases upstream compute but reduces tokens generated in peak periods. with top-5 intent prefetch turned on and a 15-minute freshness, net cost reduction ~9% beyond prefix+session, but it increases model concurrency in the precompute window.
[08:30] Maya: that's interesting, but what's the impact on throughput?
[08:33] Priya: precompute can burst GPU during windows; Optimize shows recommended burst capacity for dedicated pools or scheduled precompute off-peak. in hosted mode we recommend using rate-limited precompute jobs to avoid egress and bursting bills.
[08:49] Alex: switching tack — let's show the cost model export. i'm exporting the CSV and a quick chart of monthly delta.
[08:56] [file export noise]
[09:05] Priya: exported. baseline monthly $42k, prefix-only $36.9k, prefix+session $30.2k, hybrid+precompute $27.3k. column notes include assumptions: 55% prefix hit, session sticky 80%, avg prompt/generation tokens from your sample.
[09:28] Jordan: those numbers look compelling. what's the recommended starting configuration for a 6-week pilot?
[09:34] Priya: start with prefix 64 tokens TTL 10 min, keep batching conservative (max 4) for p95 safety, enable session KV read-only for 1 week and monitor memory; week 2-3 enable hybrid and up batch to max 6 with adaptive window. run the sandbox for 48h with production traffic mirroring to validate hit rates.
[09:56] Maya: timeline wise — we can provide the traffic heatmap by tomorrow. after that we want the sandbox the following week.
[10:03] Alex: great — we'll provision a sandbox project and share credentials. one note about quotas: sandbox has a soft spend limit but we can raise it for the POC.
[10:12] Dan: about observability — can we get token-level traces and the ability to map cost back to individual routes?
[10:18] Samir: yes, Console gives token-level breakdowns per route, model, and user; you can export traces to your Splunk/Datadog.
[10:26] Talia: any gotchas around latency when we enable encryption + session KV?
[10:30] Priya: KMS lookups add a few ms if keys are fetched per-request; we recommend caching wrapped keys in the serving layer. session KV read is local to node when affinity is used, so minimal extra latency.
[10:42] Jordan: who will support us during the POC — an SE or solutions engineer?
[10:46] Alex: priya will be the SE and i'll be the AE; we'll also loop Samir for product-level checkpoints.
[10:52] Maya: ok, last question — what do you see as the biggest risk if we proceed hosted-first?
[10:58] Samir: main risk is unexpected cache miss patterns in production traffic leading to lower-than-expected savings. that's why we run the sandbox and conservatively size batches. second is data residency if you have regulated customers — we can limit regions or offer private deployment.
[11:13] Jordan: understood. i'm comfortable with the POC approach.
[11:17] Alex: sweet. quick recap and next steps: alex to share the cost CSV, security pack, and console invite; priya to spin up sandbox and help tune TTLs; maya to share heatmap and prompt set. schedule POC scoping on 2027-05-26.
[11:34] Maya: noted. thanks everyone.
[11:36] Jordan: thanks all.
[11:38] [call ends]
